title: Playing High Society without keys; reeds
summary: He explains he mostly plays on the holes, plays High Society with no keys, and scrapes his reeds with a knife.

story.theme_name: The reed and horn player's craft: clarinet, sax, tone
story.community_name: Reeds, mouthpieces and horns: the reed player's gear

blocks.x: Well, you showed me your clarinet one time. It's 15 keys on it with a curved up bell. I noticed some of those keys don't even work anymore. You don't use all the keys? No. You work mainly with the holes in the clarinet? Yeah. Yeah, I noticed when you play high society, you don't use the keys very much. No.
You just work on the way?

Yeah, they're in the way. Yeah, they're in the way. Did you ever play a... I've got to put them on the side. Yeah. Did you ever play a clarinet with less keys than that? Did you always use that same kind of clarinet with 15 keys?
I play high society with no keys. No keys at all.
Nothing but holes. God, join me in them holes. Them things there. Yeah. His finger's right there. Yeah. His finger's right there.
What kind of a reed do you use, pig? Do you use a hard reed or a soft reed?
According to what I can master.
Do you work on it yourself if it's too hard? Do you turn it down?

Well, when it's too hard... This year tell me it's too hard. If you're blowing too hard? A soft one. Or make your reed soft. I take a little knife and just scrape a little bit on it. Ooh, a bit. Ooh. I say, I got it now. Come on, let's go. You know? Understand? Understand that.
